subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 3 – Lesson 7: English in action – Giving directions in a building
outcomes: I can ask for directions politely inside a building.
I can give directions with upstairs, along the corridor and on the left.
I can say the weak and strong forms of was and were.

tf.s: In the dialogue, it is the boy’s first visit to the shopping mall.
tf.why: He doesn’t know the mall, so he asks for directions.

tf.s: The bookshop is downstairs on the right.
tf.why: The bookshop is upstairs on the right.

tf.s: To get to the bookshop, you take the escalator to the second floor.
tf.why: It’s the second shop on the right.

tf.s: The café is on the second floor.
tf.why: The café is on the ground floor, next to the exit.

tf.s: The shoe shop is the third shop on the right.
tf.why: Go straight on; it’s the third shop on the right.

tf.s: “Can you tell me where the café is, please?” is a polite question.
tf.why: Can you tell me … please? is polite.

tf.s: In “We were visiting the bookshop”, were is strong.
tf.why: In the middle of a sentence, were is weak /wə/.

tf.s: In the short answer “Yes, I was.”, was is strong.
tf.why: At the end of a short answer, was is strong.

tf.s: “Go along the corridor” means go up in the lift.
tf.why: Along the corridor means walk down the long passage.

tf.s: The café is next to the exit.
tf.why: It’s on the left, next to the exit.

o: the third shop on the right
boxes.why: Go straight on; it’s the third shop on the right.

boxes.q: How does the boy get to the bookshop?
o: He goes out of the exit.
boxes.why: He takes the escalator to the second floor.

boxes.q: Which floor is the café on?
boxes.why: The café is on the ground floor.

boxes.q: Complete: Go ___ the corridor and around the corner.
boxes.why: We say go along the corridor.

boxes.q: Complete: It’s the first door ___ the right.
boxes.why: We say on the right / on the left.

boxes.q: Complete: Can you tell me ___ the bookshop is, please?
Which word is weak in “My sisters were waiting outside the shop”?
boxes.why: Small helping words like were are weak.

boxes.q: Is was strong or weak in “Yes, I was.”?
boxes.why: Short answers use the strong form.

boxes.q: Which three places does the boy ask about?
boxes.why: He asks for the shoe shop, the bookshop and the café.

boxes.q: Complete: Take the ___ to the first floor.
boxes.why: A lift takes you up to another floor.

hunt.q: The café is next to the…
The shoe shop is the ___ on the right.

o: On the ground floor, along the corridor and around the corner, on the left
On the second floor, on the right
mcq.why: The café is on the ground floor next to the exit.

mcq.q: Which question asks for directions politely?
o: Excuse me. Can you tell me where the bookshop is, please?
Where’s the bookshop? Tell me now!
mcq.why: Excuse me … please makes it polite.

mcq.q: When are was and were usually strong?
o: At the end, in short answers like “Yes, they were.”
Always in the middle of a sentence
mcq.why: In short answers they are strong.

mcq.q: Which phrase is NOT a direction?
mcq.why: Sorry, not now. is a reply, not a direction.

mcq.q: Correct the sentence: “The bookshop is downstairs on the right.”
o: The bookshop is upstairs on the right.
The bookshop is downstairs on the left.
The bookshop is next to the exit.
The bookshop is on the ground floor.
mcq.why: The dialogue says it is upstairs on the right.

mcq.q: Give directions to the café using “around the corner”.
o: Go along the corridor and around the corner. The café is on the left.
Go around the corner at the roof.
The café is around the ceiling.
mcq.why: Along the corridor, around the corner, then on the left.

mcq.q: Directions from the classroom: which sentence is clear and correct?
o: Go along the corridor, go down the stairs and it’s the first door on the left.
Go along the stairs on the ceiling.
It’s the first door in the left.
Go down the corridor up the roof.
mcq.why: It uses the directions language correctly.

mcq.q: The boy is on the ground floor and wants the bookshop on the second floor. What is the best direction?
o: Take the escalator to the second floor.
Go around the corner to the café.
mcq.why: He must go up two floors, so the escalator helps.

mcq.q: Why does the boy need directions?
o: It’s his first visit to the mall.
mcq.why: He doesn’t know where the shops are.

mcq.q: Which sentence has were in its weak form?
mcq.why: In the middle of a sentence, were is weak.
